uncertainties.text: Refresh token lifetime is not stated on the pages read.
Rate limits were not read on these pages.
Region or data-center hosts: the docs mention data residency, but only api_base_url_for_customer was seen.
Whether a developer instance or partner status is required just to register an app is unclear.
The Collective publishing page was blocked by a bot check, so full review requirements are unknown.
The probe was unauthenticated, so the authorize URL was only seen redirecting to sign-in. The sandbox-vs-production host split is not stated.
The registration link help.gong.io/docs/create-an-app-for-gong is a docs page, not the registration form; find the portal page where you create the app.

points.text: Apps start Private and are usable only in your own Gong account.
points.why: Gong states the app is set to Private while you create it. Publishing needs the Technology Partner Integration Review & Enablement form.

points.text: Gong says it will respond to a review request within five business days.
points.why: Gong says its team will be in touch within five business days to finalize the release and Collective listing. That is a first response, not an approval guarantee.

points.text: A developer instance request can take up to five working days.
points.why: You request it through a form. Gong's partner program appears to gate it.

points.text: Auth uses Basic client authentication and rotating refresh tokens.
points.why: The token endpoint takes Basic client_id:client_secret. A third-party source says refresh tokens are single-use.

verdict.summary: Gong offers OAuth, but customers can only install an app after a Gong Collective partner review.
